title: PowerPoint for desktop: Copilot edits presentations through chat for Copilot Chat users
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap and the conflicting Microsoft licensing statements, and its control paths and automation are documented. Two small qualifications should be added about supported Office client versions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is available to its intended Copilot Chat population without an administrator enabling it, subject to existing privacy controls.
claims.quote: Available to Copilot Chat users (without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license).

claims.claim: Group Policy Management reaches the content-analysis policy through User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: If you’re using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center.

claims.claim: UserContentDisabled set to 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the content-analysis connected-experiences policy.
claims.quote: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled 2=Disabled ... [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.where: controls[0].governs/note; Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyse content makes Copilot features unavailable in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available ... This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: Add to controls[0].note and qualify the corresponding prose: 'This applies when running the most current version of these apps.' The qualification is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy#microsoft-copilot-and-privacy-controls-for-connected-experiences.

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policy can also be configured through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policy is configured per user.
claims.quote: User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center ... [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connected experiences that analyse content are available when the governing policy is not configured.
claims.quote: If you don’t configure this policy setting, these connected experiences will be available to your users.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label GUID> -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"} configures the label's content-analysis block.
claims.quote: Set-Label -Identity "8faca7b8-8d20-48a3-8ea2-0f96310a848e" -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.claim: The label's BlockContentAnalysisServices setting has no documented portal UI and must be configured through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This configuration isn't available in the Microsoft Purview portal. You must use the PowerShell advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices with the Set-Label or New-Label cmdlet after you've connected to Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices excludes labelled content from Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
claims.quote: Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps ... Support for this setting differs for clients and apps.
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'Support differs by client and app; check the minimum supported Office versions in the sensitivity-label capabilities tables.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-office-apps#prevent-connected-experiences-that-analyze-content for this qualification.

claims.claim: Content bearing the configured sensitivity label remains available to Copilot in other scenarios such as Teams and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can select Claude in Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps when Claude is enabled.
claims.quote: In capabilities such as Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps or Researcher, users can select Claude.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft currently excludes Claude models used in Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps from the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary

claims.claim: Claude models in Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are excluded from applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Claude models are on by default for most commercial-cloud customers outside the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center route is Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences.
claims.quote: Copilot > Settings > View all ... AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors ... under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences

claims.claim: Changing the Anthropic subprocessor setting requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: No automation for assigning Anthropic subprocessor access is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic subprocessor Graph API user access settings; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph Anthropic AI provider subprocessor access settings update API. Opened connect-to-ai-subprocessor and copilot-ai-provider-user-sec-group-access; neither documents an API.

claims.where: controls[2].governs/note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Anthropic provider setting controls which users can use Claude-dependent Copilot experiences, including Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote: These assignments are applied at the provider level and enforced across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences. When access is limited by user or group membership, only the assigned users can use Copilot features or agents that rely on that AI provider.

claims.claim: Microsoft says generative AI responses are not guaranteed to be 100% factual.
claims.quote: The responses that generative AI produces aren't guaranteed to be 100% factual.
